# [CS052] Goroutine Blocked on Unbuffered Channel (goroutine-channel-leak)

A goroutine sends on an unbuffered channel that its caller may stop reading.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Reliability & Concurrency |
| **CWE** | [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) |
| **OWASP** | A06:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

When the caller returns on ctx.Done() or an early error, nobody receives the result, and the goroutine blocks forever on its send. Every timed-out request then leaks a goroutine. A buffer of one, or a select on ctx.Done() around the send, lets the goroutine finish.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
done := make(chan error)
go func() { done <- work() }()
select {
case err := <-done:
	return err
case <-ctx.Done():
	return ctx.Err()
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
done := make(chan error, 1)
go func() { done <- work() }()
select {
case err := <-done:
	return err
case <-ctx.Done():
	return ctx.Err()
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [goroutine-channel-leak]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    goroutine-channel-leak: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore goroutine-channel-leak -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** goroutine-channel-leak
```
